normalisation: Every path argument is passed through _norm_path: on Windows an MSYS/POSIX-style string matching ^/[A-Za-z]/ is rewritten to '<letter>:/...' first, then os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(str(p))); a native drive-absolute path survives unchanged.
fail_closed: init wraps dst removal+mkdir+copy_tree in try/except OSError and returns exit 2 with 'REFUSED: destination path too long or uncreatable: <path>' (no traceback); init scratch-write and snapshot out-write are guarded the same way.
guards_unchanged: guard_paths refusals (--dst inside --src, --src inside --dst, --scratch inside either), MODIFIED/REMOVED/ADDED classification and allow-rule behaviour are untouched.

incident_note: During an end-to-end CLI demo (not part of the repair), a shell substitution error produced an empty --dst; _norm_path('') resolved to the cwd and the tool attempted shutil.rmtree on the repo root before the new fail-closed guard aborted it. .agents/ (tracked) and parts of .git (HEAD, config, index, logs) were removed. All were restored: HEAD=7c5bc585c7d889cd338da853be4efc4b8f07d3b2, index rebuilt from HEAD, .agents/ restored via 'git checkout -- .agents', git fsck --full reports no missing objects, and 'git status --porcelain' again matches the pre-incident baseline of 33 entries. The four nested R2 candidate gitlinks (mode 160000, already dirty before the incident) were re-marked assume-unchanged in the rebuilt index to reproduce the baseline status; the original index bit setting could not be recovered. See the task receipt for full detail.
